Author: Rajeev Misra
Bench: Rajeev Misra
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:239717
Court No. - 65
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 48059 of 2023
Applicant :- Nazim
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Mohit Sharan Tomar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Mohammad Abid Ali,Mohd Faiz
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
1.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Mr. R.S. Tomar, Advocate, holding brief of Mr. Mohit Sharan Tomar, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State and Mr. Mohd Faiz, the learned counsel representing first informant.

2. Perused the record.
3.

This application for bail has been filed by applicant--Nazim seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 376 of 2023, under Sections 376, 323, 504, 506 IPC Police Station-Baradari,
District- Bareilly, during the pendency of trial.

Nazim vs State Of U.P. on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198056029/
1 4.

Record shows that in respect of an incident, which is alleged to have occurred on 10.04.2023 a delayed F.I.R. dated 23.05.2023 was lodged by first informant Mohd. Islam (brother of the prosecutrix) and was registered as Case Crime No. 376 of 2023, under Sections 376, 323, 504, 506,
328 I.P.C., Police Station-Baradari, District- Bareilly.

In the aforesaid F.I.R., 3 persons namely Nazim (applicant herein) Rizwana and Noor have been nominated as named accused, whereas, one unknown person (Bhabhi of Nazim) has also been arraigned as an accused.

5. The gravamen of the allegations made in the F.I.R. is to the effect that on 10.04.2023 an occurrence took place in which some poisonous substance was given to the prosecutrix i.e. the sister of the first informant on account of which she became unconscious.

The F.I.R. further records that the named accused Nazim by extending false promise of marriage repeatedly and continously dislodged the modesty of the sister of the first informant i.e. the prosecutrix for sufficiently a long time.
Ultimately, the named-accused Nazim is alleged to have refused to perform marriage with the prosecutrix.
6. After above-mentioned, F.I.R. was lodged, Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of concerned case crime number in terms of Chapter XII Cr.P.C.
The statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
Same is on record at page 30 of the paper book.
The prosecutrix in her aforesaid statements have supported the F.I.R.
She has however, stated that after 10.04.2023 named accused Nazim has refused to maintain any contact with the prosecutrix.
Subsequent to above, the prosecutrix was requested for her internal medical examination.
The prosecutrix in her statement before the doctor who medically examined her (on record at page 47 of the paper book) has supported the F.I.R.
However, the doctor who medically examined the prosecutrix did not find any injury on her body so as to denote commission of deliberate or forceful sexual assault.

With regard to the private part of the prosecutrix, the doctor has opined as follows:
Hymen- Old Torn.
7.
Ultimately, the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. which is on record at page 33 of the paper book.
The prosecutrix in her aforesaid statement has reiterated her previous statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

During course of investigation, Investigating Officer examined the first informant i.e. brother of the prosecutrix and other witnesses under Section 161 Cr.P.C. including the doctor who had medically examined her.

On the basis of above and other material collected by the Investigating Officer, during the course of investigation, he came to the conclusion that complicity of applicant Nazim alone is established in the crime in question.

He accordingly submitted the charge sheet dated 07.09.2023, whereby, applicant has been charge sheeted under Sections 376, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C.
8.
Learned counsel for applicant contends that though applicant is a named and charge-sheeted accused yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.

Attention of the Court was then invited to the F.I.R.
and the statement of the first informant recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. which is on record at page 6 of the supplementary affidavit.

With reference to above, the learned counsel for applicant submits though the F.I.R. has been lodged with a delay of 44 days, however, neither in the F.I.R. nor in the statement of the first informant referred to above, there is any explanation with regard to the Nazim vs State Of U.P. on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198056029/
2 delay in lodging the F.I.R. Placing reliance upon the judgment of Supreme Court in P. Rajagopal And Ors. Vs. The State of Tamil Nadu, AIR 2019 SC 2866/2019(5) SCC 40, learned counsel for applicant contends that since delay in lodging the F.I.R. has not been explained the prosecution of the applicant itself cannot be maintained.
9.

entities.text: P. Rajagopal And Ors. Vs. The State of Tamil Nadu, AIR 2019 SC 2866/2019(5) SCC 40
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is then contended that it is an admitted case of the prosecutrix that she was in consensual relationship with the applicant for eight long years.
However, the F.I.R. giving rise to the present criminal proceedings has been initiated after a long delay.
On the premise that the applicant has failed to solemnize marriage with the prosecutrix which was falsely extended by him to the prosecutrix.
On the above premise, the learned counsel for applicant contends that even in case of consensual relationship if there is a delay in lodging F.I.R. even then proceedings are unsustainable.

To buttress his submissions, he has referred to the following judgments of the Supreme Court:
1. Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs. State of Maharashtra (2019) 9 SCC 608.
2. Sonu @ Shubash Kumar Vs. State of U.P. 2021 SCC Online SC 181.
3. Maheshwar Tigga Vs. State of Jharkhand (2020) 10 SCC 108.
4. Deepak Mandar Pawar Vs. State of Maharashtra 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 649.
5. Naim Ahmad Vs. State (NCT of Delhi) 2023 SCC Online SC 89 10.

sentences.text: It is lastly submitted by the learned counsel for applicant that there is a difference between breach of promise and false promise of marriage.

As per the material on record the present case is a breach of promise and not false promise of marriage as nothing false was disclosed by the applicant to the prosecutrix at the begining of the consensual relationship.

It is lastly submitted that present criminal proceedings have been engineered on account of an extraneous consideration inasmuch as the applicant has already solemnized marriage with another lady in the year 2020 (i.e. 24.11.2020).
11.
Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents having no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in jail since 03.09.2023.
As such, he has undergone more than three months of incarceration.
The police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted.
Therefore, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallized.
Upto this stage, no such circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
He, therefore, submits that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case, the applicant is enlarged on bail he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
12. Per contra, the learned A.G.A.and the learned counsel representing first informant have vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
They submit that since applicant is a named and charge sheeted accused, therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.

However, they could not dislodge the factual and legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant in support of the present application for bail with reference to the record at this stage.

Nazim vs State Of U.P. on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198056029/
3 13.

Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, the learned counsel representing first informant, upon perusal of record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence,
complicity of accused and accusation made coupled with the fact that F.I.R.has been lodged with delay of 44 days, however, neither in the F.I.R. nor in the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the delay in lodging the F.I.R. has been explained, since the delay in lodging the F.I.R. has not been explained, the prosecution of applicant itself cannot be maintained,
the judgment of Supreme Court in P. Rajagopal (Supra), applicant and the prosecutrix were in consensual relationship, as per the admitted case of the prosecutrix herself the said relationship commenced eight years ago, yet the F.I.R. was lodged with delay, by reason of law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Deepak Mandar Pawar (Supra), the present criminal proceedings are unsustainable, as per the material on record, the present case is a case of breach of promise and not false promise of marriage as explained by the Apex Court in Naim Ahmad Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)
2023 SCC Online SC 89, the clean antecedents of applicant, the period of incarceration undergone,
the police report under Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C i.e. charge-sheet has already been submitted,
therefore, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallized, yet in spite of above, the learned A.G.A. and the learned counsel representing first informant could not point out any such circumstance from the record necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial, therefore, irrespective of the objections raised by the learned A.G.A. and the learned counsel representing first informant in opposition to the present application for bail, but without making any comments on the merits of the case, the applicant has made out a case for bail.
14.

2023 SCC Online SC 89
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the bail application is Allowed.

15. Let the applicant-Nazim be released on bail in aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) THE APPLICANT SHALL FILE AN UNDERTAKING TO THE EFFECT THAT HE/SHE SHALL NOT SEEK ANY ADJOURNMENT ON THE DATE FIXED FOR EVIDENCE WHEN THE WITNESSES ARE PRESENT IN COURT.
IN CASE OF DEFAULT OF THIS CONDITION, IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT IT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PASS ORDERS IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
(ii) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON EACH DATE FIXED, EITHER PERSONALLY OR THROUGH HIS/HER COUNSEL.
IN CASE OF HIS/HER ABSENCE, WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THE TRIAL COURT MAY PROCEED AGAINST HIM/HER UNDER SECTION 229-A IPC.

(iii) IN CASE, THE APPLICANT MISUSE THE LIBERTY OF BAIL DURING TRIAL AND IN ORDER TO SECURE HIS/HER PRESENCE PROCLAMATION UNDER SECTION 82 CR.P.C., MAY BE ISSUED AND IF APPLICANT FAILS TO APPEAR BEFORE THE COURT ON THE DATE FIXED IN SUCH PROCLAMATION, THEN,
Nazim vs State Of U.P. on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198056029/
4
THE TRIAL COURT SHALL INITIATE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST HIM/HER, IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW, UNDER SECTION 174-A IPC.
(iv) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT, IN PERSON, BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON DATES FIXED FOR (1) OPENING OF THE CASE, (2) FRAMING OF CHARGE AND (3) RECORDING OF STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 313 CR.P.C.

IF IN THE OPINION OF THE TRIAL COURT ABSENCE OF THE APPLICANT IS DELIBERATE OR WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THEN IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT SUCH DEFAULT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PROCEED AGAINST THE HIM/HER IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
(v) THE TRIAL COURT MAY MAKE ALL POSSIBLE EFFORTS/ENDEAVOUR AND TRY TO CONCLUDE THE TRIAL WITHIN A PERIOD OF ONE YEAR AFTER THE RELEASE OF THE APPLICANT.

16. However, it is made clear that any wilful violation of above conditions by the applicant, shall have serious repercussion on his bail so granted by this Court and the trial court is at liberty to cancel the bail, after recording the reasons for doing so, in the given case of any of the condition mentioned above.
